concept.name: Fall through the ice
concept.definition: The Wyckoff metaphor for a decisive downside break through the support ('ice') of a distribution trading range on wide price spreads and high or increasing volume, constituting a major sign of weakness and the first step of the markdown phase.
concept.intuition: The frozen floor under the market cracks and price plunges through — the downtrend has begun in earnest.
concept.mechanics: After distribution is complete, price breaks the ice with wide downside spreads, poor closes, and expanding volume, ideally pushing decisively below the support zone. The subsequent 'rally back to the ice' — a feeble recovery toward the broken support, often retracing about half the fall — is treated as the theoretically best short entry, with stops placed above the ice.
concept.failure_modes: Penetrations that lack the characteristic spread and volume, or that do not decisively clear the ice, can be shakeouts and even buying opportunities; a strong rally back through the ice zone invalidates the breakdown.
concept.misconceptions: Any tick below support is not a fall through the ice; the pattern requires a decisive break with confirming price-volume behavior, and its short-side edge depends on the character of the rally back.
concept.example: A stock's distribution range holds 136 support three times; it then drops to 128 in two sessions on heavy volume — a fall through the ice — and the analyst shorts the weak bounce to 133 with a stop above 137.

citations.source: Primary Selling Opportunity - Rally Back to the Ice (Last Point of Supply) (Wyckoff Stock Market Institute)
